title: Local paranormal investigators open up about spooky adventures
excerpt: Halloween may be the time of year when most people embrace all things spooky, but for two local ghost hunters, their interest in the unexplained goes far beyond the Halloween season.
content:
LUBBOCK, Texas — Halloween may be the time of year when most people embrace all things spooky, but for two local ghost hunters, their interest in the unexplained goes far beyond the Halloween season.

BJ Alaniz and Chelsea Aguilar grew up locally and always knew that there ways something out there.

“We like to go to places that are known to be haunted,” said Alaniz, “She shared stories with me and I shared stories with her about what I’ve experienced when I was growing up as a kid. There’s a lot that you just can’t explain.”

They’ve spent the past ten years exploring locations known for being reportedly haunted and scary, documenting their experiences and sharing them with their viewers through social media.

The duo have explored various places like Woodrow Manor, the Historic Baker Building downtown and the old Lubbock County jail. When it comes to their process, it all typically starts the same.

“We get the story, the history from the place. Most of the times, 90% of the time, it’s always going to be shadow figures, footsteps, knocks, you feel somebody touch you or something.”

From there, Alaniz said they use equipment such as electromagnetic field detectors, motion sensors and other investigative devices in an attempt to document any creepy occurrences.

Sharing it online however, can bring skepticism among viewers.

“We’ve had people say that the flashlight is remote control but everything we put out is always authentic,” Aguilar said

It’s all an experience the couple says everyone can enjoy, but only if they’re open to believing, even just for one night.

“Experience it for yourself just once. If you still don’t believe it, we won’t pressure you into believing anything that you don’t believe in. Just join us,” she said.

To see more of Aguilar and Alaniz’s adventures, you can check out their Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and Youtube. They also do ghost tours at the Historic Baker Building in downtown Lubbock, which you can find more information on the venue here.
